chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, whom should I be most righteous with?' He said, 'Your mother.' He said, 'Then who?' He said, 'Your mother.' He said, 'Then who?' He said, 'Your mother.' He said, 'Then who?' He said, 'Your father.'
ai.seo_question: Who is more deserving of kindness and righteousness, the mother or the father?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (saww) establishes the hierarchy of parental righteousness (birr al-walidayn) by tripling the emphasis on the mother, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that her physical and emotional sacrifices during pregnancy, birth, and nursing warrant superior honor. This narrative is often cited alongside the famous 'three times' tradition in Sahih Bukhari, yet Shia exegetes highlight the specific theological weight placed on maternal endurance as a precursor to paternal duty. The repetition underscores the gravity of filial piety, making the mother's status a primary pillar of Islamic ethics before extending to the father.
